@@ -57,10 +57,68 @@ jobs:
           distribution: temurin
           java-version: "21"
 
+      # Building the Flix assembly is the slowest step in the job, and it is a
+      # pure function of the flix commit, so cache it by that commit rather than
+      # rebuilding an identical jar on every release. A release that only moves
+      # the rewrite side -- or a re-run after a workflow fix -- then skips it.
+      - name: Resolve the Flix commit
+        id: flix
+        run: echo "sha=$(git -C flix rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      # Keyed on the commit with no restore-keys: a near-miss must MISS. An
+      # assembly from a different commit is not a stale cache, it is the wrong
+      # artifact, and it would be published as if it were the tagged one.
+      # The salt covers inputs the commit does not: bump it if the JDK or the
+      # build tool changes.
+      - name: Cache the Flix assembly
+        id: flix-assembly
+        uses: actions/cache@v6
+        with:
+          path: flix/out/flix/assembly.dest/out.jar
+          key: flix-assembly-jdk21-v1-${{ steps.flix.outputs.sha }}
+
       - name: Build Flix assembly
+        if: steps.flix-assembly.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
         working-directory: flix
         run: ./mill flix.assembly
 
+      # Whether it was built or restored, everything downstream assumes this jar
+      # exists and carries the decoupled front-end. Check both here, so a cache
+      # that restored partially fails now rather than as a puzzling ProGuard or
+      # scalac error later.
+      - name: Verify the Flix assembly
+        env:
+          # Passed through env rather than interpolated into the script body:
+          # ${{ }} substitution happens before bash parses anything, which is how
+          # workflow expressions turn into script injection.
+          CACHE_HIT: ${{ steps.flix-assembly.outputs.cache-hit }}
+          FLIX_SHA: ${{ steps.flix.outputs.sha }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          ASSEMBLY=flix/out/flix/assembly.dest/out.jar
+          if [ ! -s "$ASSEMBLY" ]; then
+            echo "No Flix assembly at $ASSEMBLY (cache-hit=${CACHE_HIT})." >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          # Lexer.run must not take a Flix instance. Without the decoupling the
+          # whole compiler is reachable, nothing shrinks, and the facade -- which
+          # calls the three-argument form -- does not compile.
+          #
+          # javap writes to a file before grep rather than piping into it: under
+          # `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` exits on its first match and the producer
+          # dies of SIGPIPE, so the pipeline fails exactly when the pattern IS
+          # found -- which would invert this check and let a Flix-coupled assembly
+          # through silently.
+          unzip -p "$ASSEMBLY" 'ca/uwaterloo/flix/language/phase/Lexer$.class' > "Lexer.class"
+          "${JAVA_HOME}/bin/javap" -p "Lexer.class" > lexer-signatures.txt
+          if grep -qE 'run\(.*api\.Flix' lexer-signatures.txt; then
+            echo "The tagged Flix commit does not carry the Lexer/Parser2 decoupling." >&2
+            echo "Tag the flix fork at a commit that does; see the README." >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "assembly ok ($(du -h "$ASSEMBLY" | cut -f1), flix ${FLIX_SHA})"
+
       # Build the published parser jar: compile the pure-Java facade against the
       # assembly, merge it in, then shrink from the facade as the only root.
       #
